name: stats-dashboard
description: Reporting page composing a KPI row (the grid primitive filled with stats) and card panels, one of which holds the table recipe with its formatting contract — data-format columns, data-value cells and a live-aggregating tfoot. Composition only: this pattern ships no JavaScript of its own; loading faqir-core.js (which bundles table.js) makes the table sortable and its totals live.

heading.description: Report title. Give it an id and point the section's aria-labelledby at it

description.description: Optional intro paragraph. Must be a direct child of the section — the panels' own card descriptions are card slots, not this one

period.description: The reporting period and its comparison basis, e.g. '1–30 June 2026 · compared with May'. Rendered as muted metadata, not prose

metrics.description: The KPI row. It is itself a data-ui='grid', so the column count comes from grid's mobile-first vocabulary — data-cols='1' is the phone base and data-cols-md/data-cols-lg widen it (1 → 2 → 4); the stats inside carry no data-part

reports.description: Region holding the report panels. Two sit side by side (2fr 1fr); a single one spans the full width

report.description: One report panel — a nested data-ui='card'. Inside it you address the CARD's slots (header, title, description, body, footer), never this pattern's: the nearest data-ui ancestor owns a data-part. Named `report` rather than `panel` because the audit's aria-describedby rule treats a [data-part='panel'] as a dialog's describable surface

footnote.description: Fine print under the report panels (what the numbers exclude, how they are counted)

default.description: The only state — a report renders what it was given; loading and error states belong to whatever fetches the data

required_attrs: aria-labelledby on the section pointing at the heading id
aria-labelledby on each report panel pointing at its own title id
a <caption> on every report table saying what it counts and over which period
scope='col' on every table header cell
the trend of a stat is stated in its change text, not only by the data-trend colour

keyboard.Tab: move through the report panel links and, once table.js is loaded, the sortable column headers

templates.html:
{heading}

{description}

{period}

{metric_label} {metric_value} {metric_change}

{panel_title}

{table_caption}
{column} {amount_column}
{row_label} {row_amount_formatted}
{total_label} {total}

{footnote}

data_shape.note: What an agent binds where. The pattern is static markup — these are the shapes to render into it, whether server-side or through l-for over an l-source.

item.label: string — what is measured ([data-part='label'])
item.change: string — the comparison, stated in words ([data-part='change'])
item.trend: 'up' | 'down' | 'neutral' — data-trend on the stat; it colours the change, so the change text must still say which way it went

item.cells: one [data-part='td'] per column, in header order
item.data-value: the RAW number on numeric cells (unformatted, dot decimal). table.js re-renders the cell through Intl using data-format plus data-locale/data-currency on the table root; the authored text is the no-JS fallback
item.data-format: 'number' | 'currency' | 'percent' | 'date' — must match the column header's data-format
item.note: body cells never opt into aggregation — a tfoot cell reads its whole column by index, so adding data-aggregate here does nothing

item.data-aggregate: 'sum' | 'avg' | 'min' | 'max' | 'count' — recomputed over the VISIBLE body rows of one column (filtered-out rows are excluded)
item.data-col: zero-based index of the column to read. Without it the cell aggregates its own position, which only holds when the footer row's cells line up with the body's
item.text: the authored total, which stands when no controller is loaded

notes: Slot ownership: a data-part belongs to its nearest data-ui ancestor. The KPI row is data-ui='grid', so the stats inside it must NOT carry a data-part — it would become an orphan part of the grid, which declares no slots. That is the deliberate trade: composing the grid buys the responsive column collapse and costs the per-metric part. Address a KPI as [data-part='metrics'] > [data-ui='stat'].
Same rule inside a report panel: the panel IS the card, so its title/description/body/footer are the CARD's slots and a stats-dashboard part there would be an orphan part of the card.

The report table is the table recipe unchanged — this pattern's stylesheet defines no table rules beyond letting it scroll sideways inside the panel. Column formatting is the recipe's contract: data-format on the th, data-value + matching data-format on the td, data-aggregate on the column's body cells, and the tfoot cell that totals them.

The authored numbers are the no-JS truth. table.js reformats data-value cells through Intl and recomputes data-aggregate footers over the visible rows once faqir-core.js is loaded, so the two must agree when the page ships — tests/patterns/stats-dashboard.test.ts adds up each aggregated column and compares it with the authored total.

Aggregation is declared in the tfoot alone: the footer cell names the column with data-col and reads every visible body cell in it. The body cells carry only data-value plus their column's data-format.

changes.note: The responsive ladder moves onto the breakpoint canon, mobile-first (task 0.8-09). The sheet's max-width media blocks became min-width floors on canon tiers (sm 40rem/640px, md 48rem/768px, lg 64rem/1024px), so every unconditional rule is now the PHONE case and a tier block only ever widens it. The panel region stacks until lg; the KPI row's own ladder was already grid.css's. The floors keep their values, so the only behavioural shift is at exactly a floor: 1024px now gets the wide layout rather than the narrow one.
